data.name: result
data.shape: OpenProposalResult — proposal (consequence, dispositions, confirmationToken) | no-op | not-possible | stale | resolved | unreadable | not-found
data.source: app.openProposal.execute — describes at the moment of opening, never from recorded values

data.name: problem
data.source: searchParams — the refusal a bounced agree returned with

components.purpose: The ceremony's beginning: what agreeing would do, computed against the account as it is right now.
components.current_implementation: Every branch renders through the shared Shell (max-w-3xl, space-y-4, p-6, back-link to /pending). Refusal branches are prose sentences; each says why and offers no control — 'a disabled button still implies the change is available'.
constraints: Every branch that cannot be agreed to says why and offers NO control — never a disabled one (in-code ruling, and the mcp-control scenario 'The change is no longer possible').
The describe runs at open time; nothing on this page may render a consequence computed when the proposal was recorded (requirement: A Proposal Is Agreed To Against The World As It Is Then).

components.purpose: The frame every branch shares, carrying the refusal a bounced agree returned with.
components.current_implementation: h1, underlined back-link, then the problem in the danger role with a semibold 'Refused:' prefix (role=alert) — rendered here so the refusal survives whichever branch the redirect lands on. Landed by a-bounced-agree-says-why.
constraints: The problem renders on EVERY branch — a bounced agree can land on a page that now describes a different state.
role=alert and the verbatim reason must survive.

components.purpose: What agreeing would do, in the product's one consequence vocabulary.
components.current_implementation: h2 'What agreeing would do' plus the consequence sentence as an unstyled text-base paragraph — the same sentence the web-initiated change renders, but without the consequence role the archive confirmation gives it (DT-0004).
constraints: The consequence sentence is the product's own for this write and renders verbatim — 'this page must not grow a second vocabulary for the same write'.
Consequence outranks everything on a screen (system.json principle).

components.purpose: What was proposed beside what will actually happen — both, always; a page that merges them agrees on the operator's behalf.
components.current_implementation: Setting/Proposed/What-happens table in a rounded-gc-2 border-border-default scroll container; dispositions named in words (will change / already the case / not accepted). The departs warning and the nothing-would-change conclusion are unstyled paragraphs.
constraints: Every proposed value is listed whatever became of it — dropping an already-true value under-reports the proposal, omitting a refused one over-reports it.
Dispositions are named in words, never by colour alone.
The departs warning renders before the table — a reader who stops at the first sentence must still learn this is not what was suggested.
The table stays inside its own overflow-x-auto container.

components.purpose: The committing half of the decision: perform the ordinary write with the ordinary confirmation.

actions.effect: Server action: updateAgent with the minted confirmationToken; success closes the proposal and lands on /pending; a refusal bounces back here with ?problem=

components.current_implementation: BUTTON_PRIMARY submit, 'Agree and make this change'; hidden inputs carry id, target, token and the proposed values.
constraints: Offered only on the proposal branch — never on no-op or any refusal branch.
Goes through the same confirm-and-perform path as a web-initiated change (mcp-control scenario).

components.purpose: The other half of the decision — an operation, not a footnote; it closes the proposal for good.

actions.effect: Server action: resolves the proposal declined; nothing is written to the account

components.current_implementation: BUTTON_SECONDARY submit in its own form, labeled 'Decline — this closes the proposal permanently'.
constraints: A visible peer of agree, never a text link — 'a text link beneath the agree button read as the way out of the page rather than the other half of the decision'.
The permanence stays in the label.

components.current_implementation: Shared NotConnected component; treatment owned by DT-0006.

flows.name: Agree
steps: read the consequence and the difference
land on /pending with the proposal closed

flows.name: A refused agree
steps: return here with the reason in the Refused banner
the page re-describes against the world as it now is

accessibility.notes: The problem banner carries role=alert. Dispositions are legible without colour. No client JS.
